title: Automation, Income Incidence, and Capital Accumulation in Incomplete Markets
summary: This paper studies how automation changes the stationary distribution of income, consumption, and wealth in an incomplete-market economy. An automating sector trades off productivity gains and labor-cost savings against adoption costs. Households differ by skill and wealth, save in a capital/equity claim, and face uninsurable skill risk. Competitive factor prices and aggregate capital clear jointly with household Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equations and the stationary Kolmogorov forward equation.
